title: Finitely presented Zariski main finite factorization
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated, quasi-finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [pqf-def-quasifinite], with $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Assume $f$ is of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exist a scheme $T$, a quasi-compact open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a finite morphism $p:T\to S$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of finite presentation such that $f=p\circ j$. The scheme $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0F2N, label lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite-addendum; includes the factorization of the preceding lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite, with qcqs finite factor over qcqs S

proof.text: A finite presentation $R$-algebra $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ is generated by the images of the $x_a$. Thus local finite presentation gives local finite type, and the assumed quasi-compactness makes $f$ of finite type. Apply [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to this separated, everywhere quasi-finite $f$ over the qcqs $S$. Obtain $X\xrightarrow{j_0}T_0\xrightarrow{p_0}S$ with $j_0$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $p_0$ finite and $p_0j_0=f$.

source.place: Tag 0F2N, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite-addendum, preceding Lemma 05K0 supplies the initial factorization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-fp-approximation] to $p_0:T_0\to S$. Choose its directed system $T_i$, maps $p_i$ and projections $\pi_i$. The stages are finite and of finite presentation over $S$, the transitions are closed immersions, and $p_i\pi_i=p_0$.

Finite morphisms are affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] to $p_0$ and all $p_i$: they are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] over the qcqs $S$ makes $T_0$ and every $T_i$ qcqs. The same clause applied to the assumed quasi-compact $f$ makes $X$ quasi-compact, so its open image $j_0(X)$ is a quasi-compact open of $T_0$.

source.place: Tag 0F2N, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite-addendum, hypotheses for open descent, written out

proof.text: Each closed transition is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc](b). Apply [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends](1),(3) to $T_0=\varprojlim T_i$ and the quasi-compact open $j_0(X)$. Choose a quasi-compact open $U_i\subset T_i$ whose inverse image is $j_0(X)$; on the tail $k\ge i$ put $U_k=r_{ki}^{-1}(U_i)$. The restricted projections identify $X$ with $\varprojlim_{k\ge i}U_k$, and every $U_k$ is quasi-compact. Transitions $U_l\to U_k$ are the restrictions of closed immersions: over an affine chart a quotient $A\to A/J$ remains a quotient after localization, so these restrictions are closed immersions. All restricted projections remain morphisms over $S$.

For each $k$, $p_k$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type by the generator argument in step 1. Its restriction $U_k\to S$ is locally of finite type: inside any finite-type affine chart, take distinguished opens contained in $U_k$; their coordinate rings $B_h$ are generated by the generators of $B$ and $h^{-1}$. This verifies the local finite type hypothesis without assuming $S$ Noetherian. The induced limit morphism is the original $f$, which is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-limit-lfp-stabilization] to the tail system $U_k$. For some $k\ge i$ the canonical $S$-map $e:X\to U_k$ is an isomorphism.

Set $T=T_k$, $p=p_k$, and $j$ equal to $e$ followed by the open inclusion $U_k\hookrightarrow T_k$. This is an open immersion, and $pj=f$ because $e$ is the restricted projection $\pi_kj_0$ and $p_k\pi_kj_0=p_0j_0$. By step 2, $p$ is finite and of finite presentation; by step 3, $T$ is qcqs. The source $X$ is quasi-compact and $T$ quasi-separated, so clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] gives quasi-compactness of $j$. This proves every requested clause, including the explicit qcqs assertion on the existential scheme.
